{{Quote|One night on our plodding journey we were visited by what I can only call fairylights at our evening campfires. These tiny, luminous flying creatures come out at night with buzzing, squeaking noises.|Pfilbee Jhorn|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
'''Wisties''', also called '''firefolk''', '''flutterglows''' or '''firesprites''', were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the forest moon of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. They were very small, winged [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that had the appearance of a moving [[Fire/Legends|flame]]. However, fire did not have anything to do with [[Bioluminescence/Legends|their luminosity]], and they could be safely touched by other creatures most of the [[Time/Legends|time]]. Although the Wisties seemed extremely simple, even non-sentient, they had a [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Wistie language|their own]] and even a form of government, with a [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] as [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]]. It was thought that the firefolk fed off happy emotions and expressions of mirth.

They were known offworld as early as [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], in the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Because of their beauty and rarity, the firefolk fetched high prices on the illegal market. Despite that, knowledge of their existence was not very widespread in the [[galactic community]]: when [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] [[Pfilbee Jhorn]] encountered Wisties on an expeditionary mission after [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], he did not recognize them and even doubted they were actual creatures. During the time when most of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] was ruled by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Izrina]] was Queen of the Wisties.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|We could not tell for certain what the fairylights eat, or even whether they are true life-forms rather than just strange light phenomena.|Pfilbee Jhorn|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
[[File:Izrina-TheCriesOfTheTrees.png|thumb|left|The Wisties were tiny winged humanoids]]
The Wisties of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] were tiny [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with one head, a torso, two [[Limb/Legends|legs]] and two arms, with the latter ending in three-<ref name="CotT" /> or four-fingered hands.<ref name="CC:EA" /> Some individuals had no visible digits.<ref name="E:SOE">''[[Star Wars: Ewoks—Shadows of Endor]]''</ref> They were surrounded by a bright mantle of fluttering [[Fire/Legends|flames]],<ref name="DBiz">{{DB|character|queenizrina|Izrina, Queen}}</ref> the [[Color/Legends|color]] of which could be [[Gold/Legends|golden]], white,<ref name="CC:EA" /> red,<ref name="E1A7" /> or blue. Their mask-like faces featured two forward-facing [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and a large [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] relative to their size.<ref name="CotT" /> Some Wisties had a [[Hair/Legends|hair]]-like corona of light sprouting from the top of their head. While they seemed to "flicker" as a flame would do&mdash;and sometimes even seemed to disappear for split second&mdash;<ref name="CC:EA" /> they were well and truly corporeal, and could be restrained with the help of miniature chains.<ref name="CotT" /> They were so small that they could fit in the palm of an Ewok.<ref name="CC:EA" /> All known Wisties were referred to as [[Gender/Legends|females]] in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]],<ref name="CotT" /><ref name="CC:EA" /><ref name="E1A7" /> the most prominent [[Language/Legends|language]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

The Wisties rarely kept still, which rendered detailed examination of their body features difficult. Most of the [[Time/Legends|time]], they appeared more like thin lines of light that flew in the air erratically,<ref name="CC:EA" /> which prompted uninformed observers to think they were unexplained light phenomena.<ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> Because of their spark-like appearance, they were often called "the firefolk" or "the flutterglows" by the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], a race of one [[Meter/Legends|meter]] tall [[Bear/Legends|bear]]-like sentients with whom they shared their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Their luminescence, however, was not [[Fire/Legends|fire]]-based, but [[Bioluminescence/Legends|biochemical]].<ref name="DBiz" /> Although they did emit [[Temperature/Legends|heat]], which was fanned through the rapid beating of their wings and produced light,<ref name="COE" /> they could normally be touched by other organics without risk.<ref name="CC:EA" /> However, angered Wisties could increase their body heat to such a degree that their could actually burn.<ref name="COE" /> They also had the ability to transfer some of their energy to certain responsive objects, including [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitive]] [[gem]]stones like the [[Sunstar/Legends|Sunstar]].<ref name="E:SOE" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Swarms of them were attracted by fires and our presence. We tried to shoo them away, but nothing seemed to work, and the things continued to pester us long into the darkness.|Pfilbee Jhorn|<ref name="ISWU" />}}
[[File:Wisties.jpg|thumb|A swarm of Wisties]]
Wisties lived in swarms of several dozens individuals. At night, those swarms would venture in the open air,<ref name="CC:EA" /> where they performed what has been described as "flashing, spinning, dizzying light shows." During their aerial ballets, the firefolk were usually peaceful and harmless, although their buzzing and brightly lit night flights could prevent other beings from sleeping, much to their annoyance and discomfort.<ref name="ISWU" /> In the rare cases when a Wistie got angry, it could increase its internal heat greatly, allowing the creature to burn through traps and nets.<ref name="COE" />

===Diet===
{{Quote|I think she eats giggles.''"<br />"''They're giggles-eaters!|Mace and Cindel Towani|<ref name="CC:EA" />}}
Observers were uncertain as to what the Wisties [[Diet/Legends|ate]]. Although their behavior indicated that they absorbed firelight as a source of nourishment, some believed that they fed on laughters and other manifestations of warm feelings.<ref name="ISWU" /> In any event, the Wisties were indeed fond of laughter, and appeared to possess some ability to either physically or psychically affect other beings in a manner that provoked it. The sensation has been compared to playful tickling. The experience was considered extremely enjoyable and continued to be so long after an actual tickling would have become unpleasant.<ref name="CC:EA" /> Once deprived of her liberty for an extended period, a Wistie was in imminent danger of [[Death/Legends|dying]] of starvation.<ref name="E:SOE" />

===Relations with other Endorians===
{{Quote|This is the best Wistie Fest ever!|[[Chief/Legends|Chief]] [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]]|<ref name="FAAE" />}}
[[File:Wistie_and_Ewoks.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Wisties and Ewoks playing together]]
The spark-like beings generally maintained cordial relations with the tree-dwelling Ewoks, who even had a holiday in their honor, called the [[Festival of the Wisties]]. Both species would celebrate that event together in a playful atmosphere, performing a [[Wistie Dance|dance]] and baking a [[Wistie Fest pie|special pie]] made from [[Rainbow berry|rainbow berries]].<ref name="FAAE">''[[Fuzzy as an Ewok: Things to See, Touch, and Smell from the Forest Moon of Endor]]''</ref> Wisties and young Ewoks would often frolic together in the forests or on the edges of a pond.<ref name="COE" /> Despite that, even their Ewok friends still regarded the untimely night flights of the firefolk as a nuisance, at least in the context of camp life.<ref name="CC:EA" /> By contrast, the Wisties were prey to the warlike [[Dulok/Legends|Duloks]], the lankier cousins of the Ewoks, who considered them delicacies<ref name="CotT" /> and sometimes caged them into small lanterns.<ref name="E:SOE" />

Wisties normally spoke [[Wistie language|their own language]], which was made of squeaking and buzzing noises.<ref name="ISWU" /> Some Ewoks, including [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]]<ref name="CotT" /> and later [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa]]<ref name="E:SOE" /> were able to understand that language.<ref name="CotT" /> Conversely, a few Wisties who had been taken offworld also showed the ability to speak Galactic Basic Standard fluently.<ref name="E1A7" />

==History==
===Early encounters===
{{Quote|Yes! I had time alone, free from my tribe. I listened to no voices but mine and the Wisties in the trees.|Treek|<ref name="SWTOR" />}}
[[File:Moon_of_Endor_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|150px|The Forest Moon of Endor, homeworld of the Wisties]]
The Wisties were [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to Endor, a forested moon in orbit around the planet of the [[Endor (planet)/Legends|same name]], in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> They shared their homeworld with several other intelligent or semi-intelligent species, namely the Ewoks, the Duloks, the [[fftssfft]]<ref name="COE" /> the [[Yuzzum/Legends|Yuzzums]],<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and the [[Gorph/Legends|Gorphs]].<ref name="PriLat">{{Ewoks|Princess Latara}}</ref> As early as [[3640 BBY]] the firefolk and their bear-like neighbors knew each other, as the Ewok [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] named [[Treek/Legends|Treek]] mentioned how she liked to listen to the Wisties in the forest.<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''</ref> The firefolk's first encounters with the wider [[galactic community]] dated back to at least [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], in the waning decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. By that date, several Wisties had been abducted by offworld visitors and sold as living trinkets elsewhere in the galaxy.<ref name="E1A7" />

Some time after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Wisties encountered [[Pfilbee Jhorn]], a [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] who had been requisitioned for an expeditionary mission to Endor. The flutterglows were attracted by the Imperial campfires, and they started to fly around their visitors, as they usually did. The Imperials tried to shoo them away, but to no avail. As records officer of the expedition, Jhorn reported that encounter in his field journal.<ref name="ISWU" />

===Morag's plot===
{{Quote|From you fire shall spread the forest's death. Mmuahahaha!|Morag|<ref name="CotT" />}}
[[File:Morag7.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Morag releasing the cursed Izrina, Queen of the Wisties]]
Around [[3 ABY/Legends|3.5 ABY]], the fairy-folk of Endor were ruled over by [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Izrina]]. One day, the Queen fell prey of [[Morag]], a mandrill-faced [[Tulgah/Legends|Tulgah]] witch who dwelled on Endor. Morag used her arcane [[Magic/Legends|magic]] to put Izrina into a state of perpetual anger, rendering her able to set things aflame through casual contact. When the Queen travelled back to her home, she infected her fellow Wisties with Morag's curse. Because of Morag's wicked ruse, the erratic flight of the Wisties caused a terrible forest fire that nearly destroyed the [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] and, more importantly, the sacred [[Soul Tree]]s of the Ewoks.<ref name="CotT" />

However, even as the Ewoks struggled to fight the fire, they found a way to free the firefolk from Morag's spell, when the young warrior [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]] doused Izrina with [[Water/Legends|water]]. Wicket and his friends then cured the rest of the Wisties, and put out the remaining fires with the help of magic foam concocted by [[Logray/Legends|Logray]] the [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]]. In gratitude, the firefolk offered to help implement Warrick's plan to airdrop Logray's firefoam by guiding the Ewok [[Hang-glider/Legends|skin gliders]] safely around the dangerous convection currents caused by the forest fire. As a result, the fire was quickly brought under control and the wisties took the liberty of dropping a bag of firefoam on Morag to humiliate her in revenge.<ref name="CotT" />

===Meeting the Caravan of Courage===
[[File:Wistie_swarm.png|thumb|A swarm of Wisties flying around an Ewok campfire]]
{{Quote|Wisties! Wisties!|Wicket W. Warrick|<ref name="CC:EA" />}}
Shortly afterwards, when an Ewok caravan accompanied the young [[Human/Legends|Humans]] [[Mace Towani|Mace]] and [[Cindel Towani]] in their search for their [[Parent/Legends|parents]] camped in the Endor plains, a group of Wisties were attracted by the campfires. The young Cindel then presented [[Candle of Pure Light]], a magical artifact provided by Logray, and the Wisties all leaped into its flame. That event had the consequence of summoning Queen Izrina, who decided to accompany the caravan. She later proved helpful in distracting a malevolent [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]] while the Ewoks rescued the elder Towani from that creature's lair.<ref name="CC:EA" />

==Wisties in the galaxy==
[[File:GTHpalace.jpg|thumb|left|Around 32 BBY, a swarm of captured Wisties lived in the palace of Gardulla the Hutt.]]
To outlanders, the Wisties gained numerous nicknames, such as firefolk,<ref name="DBiz" /> firesprites<ref name="COE" /> or flutterglows.<ref name="DBiz" /> Their existence was known to other species since at least 32 BBY. Around that year, a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime boss]] named [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla]] had imported Wisties in the [[Gardulla's pleasure garden|pleasure garden]] of [[Imperial Station Bravo|her palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Although those Wisties lived in an environment close to their natural habitat, they still were [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to the Hutt. When Gardulla opened her garden to night parties, the Wisties served as flying night-lights.<ref name="E1A7" /> Indeed, the Wisties were often captured and put on the black market because of their extreme beauty and rarity, which contributed to reduce their number on Endor.<ref name="COE" /> Around [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> a gray-haired Human who was part of a resistance movement on [[Samaria/Legends|Samaria]] went by the nickname of "[[Firefolk]]." Although it may have been a coincidence, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ferus Olin]] found it amusing that a grown man would have chosen the name of a tiny, glowing creature.<ref name="LJ6" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Wistie species first appeared in the [[1984]] movie ''[[Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure]]'', a made-for-TV film set in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' galaxy. They were also featured in two episodes of the animated TV series [[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']], which ran from [[1985]] to [[1986]]. The first one, titled "[[The Cries of the Trees]]," had its plot revolve around Morag's attempt to burn down the forest by hexing the Wisties. The opening credits of the [[Ewoks: Season Two|second season]] also featured original footage of Wisties hovering around the show's typographic logo.

[[File:Willow_fairies.png|thumb|Fairy-like beings also appeared in Ron Howard's ''Willow'', co-written by ''Star Wars'' creator George Lucas.]]
In [[1988]], four years after the release of ''Caravan of Courage'', the creator of ''Star Wars'' [[George Lucas]] wrote the story of [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']], a [[Wikipedia:Fantasy film|fantasy film]] directed by [[Ron Howard]]. The movie featured Cherlindrea and her people of tiny, glowing fairies, which were very similar to Wisties of the ''Star Wars'' universe.<ref name="fairies">[[Willow (film)|''Willow'']]</ref> The Wisties also share similarities with the will-o'-the wisp from European folklore, which were ghostly, flickering lights that could be seen hovering over swamps and bogs and were believed to lure travelers of their routes.<ref name="will'o">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-imagination-mythological-creatures-in-star-wars-part-2|text=Drawing from the Imagination: Mythological Creatures in ''Star Wars'', Part 2|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref>

The subtitles of the ''Caravan of Courage'' DVD used the alternate spelling "Whistie."
